subject: Urban Planning
title: Height Limits: How Tall Can You Build?
description: Learn Height Limits: How Tall Can You Build? in one minute.

hook.text: Washington, D.C. limits all buildings to 130 feet — roughly 12 stories. It's been the law since 1910.

buildup.text: The Height Act was passed so no building would tower over the Capitol dome. The city's skyline is deliberately flat.

discovery.text: The result: D.C. is one of the most expensive housing markets in America. Limited height means limited supply.

twist.text: Paris has similar height limits. But Paris has seven times D.C.'s density because it allows midrise everywhere.

climax.text: Height isn't the only path to density. Consistent midrise buildings across a city house more people than scattered towers.

punchline.text: You don't need skyscrapers for density. You need six stories on every block.

quiz.question: Why is D.C. expensive despite having a height limit?
options: The height limit restricts housing supply in a high-demand city
Federal government buildings take up most available land
D.C. charges the highest property taxes in the country
